question: Which organ is in the greatest danger during a paracetamol overdose?

options.A: The stomach
options.B: The kidneys
options.C: The liver
options.D: The pancreas

explanation: The liver works hard to break down paracetamol. When too much is taken at once, it gets overwhelmed and can suffer serious damage.

question: What should you do immediately after a drain is successfully pulled out from a surgical wound?

options.A: Ask the patient to stand up and walk around the room
options.B: Leave the small hole open to the air so it dries quickly
options.C: Wash the open tract thoroughly with harsh antiseptic soap
options.D: Apply a sterile, airtight dressing over the insertion site

explanation: Always seal the site immediately with an airtight sterile dressing to protect the healing tissue and stop any air leaks or bleeding.

question: What are the three main functions of the nervous system?

options.A: Digestion, absorption, and elimination
options.B: Sensory input, integration, and motor output
options.C: Protection, support, and movement
options.D: Circulation, respiration, and excretion

explanation: The nervous system constantly gathers information, processes it in the brain and spinal cord, and sends out commands to the body. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T1#GNS222_U3_T1_h1)

question: A patient has been convulsing for eight minutes straight without waking up. What is your immediate nursing priority?

options.A: Wait quietly at the bedside until the patient stops moving on their own
options.B: Have the patient stand up and walk around to clear their head
options.C: Call for emergency medical help and prepare airway support and rescue medication
options.D: Ask the family members what the patient ate for breakfast

explanation: This is a true emergency! Prolonged seizures cut off vital oxygen to the brain, so you need to sound the alarm and grab rescue medication right away.

question: Why do international agreements like the Cairo Programme of Action matter for local Nigerian nursing practice?

options.A: They allow nurses to bypass local hospital rules during emergency obstetric procedures
options.B: They eliminate the need for patient consent in family planning clinics
options.C: They legally require international organizations to fund all local nursing salaries
options.D: They provide a standard framework that governments use to shape national health policies and clinic guidelines

explanation: Big global agreements help shape our national laws and clinic guidelines, which directly guide the safe and effective care you will provide to your patients.

question: A community midwife in a remote village is treating a woman with severe bleeding after childbirth who needs a blood transfusion. What should she do first?

options.A: Stabilize the patient with available fluids and arrange an immediate emergency referral
options.B: Ask the family members to perform minor surgery in the clinic ward
options.C: Wait until morning before telling anyone about the excessive bleeding
options.D: Discharge the patient immediately to free up the hospital bed

explanation: You've got this! When an emergency is beyond the clinic's capacity, stabilize the patient with what you have and arrange a swift transfer to a higher center.

question: What happens first during the assessment phase of the nursing process?

options.A: Evaluating whether the patient has achieved their health goals
options.B: Writing the final medical diagnosis for the patient's chart
options.C: Collecting subjective and objective data about the patient's health status
options.D: Administering prescribed medications and performing wound care procedures

explanation: Assessment is always step one! It's like being a detective—gathering clues by talking to the patient, doing a physical check, and looking at lab results.

question: Why does unequal household power make it harder for some women to get healthcare?

options.A: It forces female patients to work in hazardous industrial environments
options.B: It automatically increases the physiological risk of contracting infectious diseases
options.C: It prevents women from independently seeking or funding their own medical care
options.D: It stops hospitals from hiring female doctors and nurses

explanation: If a woman has no control over household money and needs permission just to leave the house, getting to a clinic when she's sick becomes a massive hurdle.

question: Which lab test is primarily used to monitor a patient who is taking heparin?

options.A: Prothrombin Time (PT)
options.B: Serum electrolyte panel
options.C: Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time (aPTT)
options.D: Total red blood cell count

explanation: We use the aPTT test to keep a close eye on heparin therapy and make sure our patient's blood is clotting at a safe, therapeutic level.

question: What must mothers avoid putting on a newborn baby's umbilical cord stump?

options.A: Clean air and dry gauze
options.B: Traditional concoctions, saliva, or oils
options.C: Recommended antiseptic solutions
options.D: Clean water and mild soap

explanation: Putting unsterile substances like herbs, saliva, or oils on the cord introduces nasty bacteria and tetanus spores. Keep it clean and dry instead!

question: What is a major benefit of involving local community leaders in reproductive health programs?

options.A: It allows community members to perform complex surgical operations
options.B: It builds local ownership and encourages people to use health services early
options.C: It eliminates the requirement for government funding in hospitals
options.D: It removes the need for trained nurses in rural health posts

explanation: When community leaders are involved, people trust the program more, drop harmful myths, and come to the clinic early for help. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T2#GNS312_U5_T2_h8)

question: At what angle should an intramuscular injection be inserted into the skin?

options.A: 45 degrees
options.B: 90 degrees
options.C: 15 degrees
options.D: 30 degrees

explanation: A perpendicular 90-degree angle ensures the needle penetrates deep enough to reach the muscle layer beneath the skin and fat. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T6#GNS125_U3_T6_h4)

question: What is the medical term for the patchy, purplish skin color that appears on the hands and feet when circulation slows down?

options.A: Cyanosis
options.B: Jaundice
options.C: Mottling
options.D: Erythema

explanation: Mottling happens when blood flow slows way down, causing blood to pool in the hands and feet with a purplish, blotchy pattern. Keep up the good work!

question: Why do we count water as a nutrient even though it gives us zero calories?

options.A: It breaks down into simple sugars inside the stomach lining
options.B: It is essential for life, acting as a medium for all metabolic reactions
options.C: It stimulates the production of digestive enzymes in the pancreas
options.D: It converts directly into structural tissue during growth phases

explanation: Correct! A nutrient is anything needed for survival and body chemistry—it doesn't have to provide energy to be vital.

question: What is an essential safety habit after calculating a children's drug dose?

options.A: Throw away half of the calculated medication
options.B: Heat the liquid to body temperature before giving
options.C: Ask another nurse to double-check the math
options.D: Store the leftover mixture in a dark refrigerator

explanation: Two pairs of eyes are always better than one, especially with kids' doses! A quick double-check keeps everyone safe and builds your clinical confidence.

question: How can community health nurses best encourage rural women to seek early help for breast lumps?

options.A: By distributing expensive mammogram machines to every household
options.B: By banning traditional healers from practicing any form of medicine
options.C: By engaging local leaders and providing culturally sensitive education
options.D: By waiting quietly in the hospital clinic for patients to walk in

explanation: Working hand-in-hand with village leaders and using simple, warm language builds trust and brings women to the clinic early.

question: How do nursing theorists define 'health' within our professional framework?

options.A: A dynamic state of physical, mental, and social well-being
options.B: The complete elimination of all hospital admissions nationwide
options.C: The total absence of any identifiable bacteria in the blood
options.D: A static condition achieved strictly through pharmaceutical drugs

explanation: Health isn't just the literal absence of sickness. In nursing, we see it as a flowing, everyday state of overall physical, mental, and social well-being. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h4)

question: Which action shows the best emotional support for a patient dealing with infertility?

options.A: Telling the patient to stop worrying because everything happens for a reason
options.B: Listening actively and validating the patient's emotional grief
options.C: Avoiding the topic of children during all health conversations
options.D: Focusing solely on physical medication administration schedules

explanation: Well done! Infertility brings deep emotional pain. Listening without judgment helps patients process their grief in a safe space.

question: What test is mainly used to check for a broken bone after a bad joint injury?

options.A: Urinalysis
options.B: Electrocardiogram
options.C: Complete blood count
options.D: X-ray imaging

explanation: An X-ray gives a clear picture of the bones, helping doctors easily rule out a fracture when a patient comes in with severe trauma.

question: Why must patients with liver disease avoid taking casual painkillers like paracetamol without asking a doctor?

options.A: It neutralizes the effects of prescribed lactulose syrup
options.B: The liver has to process it, and it can cause more damage
options.C: It causes severe allergic skin rashes in liver patients
options.D: It increases the risk of dehydration and kidney failure

explanation: Medications like paracetamol are processed by the liver. When the liver is weak, these drugs can build up quickly and cause serious harm.

question: How does health promotion differ from basic disease treatment?

options.A: It relies entirely on expensive surgical interventions
options.B: It focuses on environmental conditions and empowerment rather than just fixing illness
options.C: It is handled exclusively by doctors in private clinics
options.D: It only applies to children and elderly populations

explanation: While disease treatment steps in after sickness occurs, health promotion looks at the bigger social and living conditions that keep people well in the first place. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h1)

question: What is the danger of giving a central cough suppressant to a patient who has a chest full of thick mucus?

options.A: The mucus instantly dissolves into clear water.
options.B: Blood pressure drops to dangerous levels.
options.C: Mucus can accumulate and block the airways.
options.D: The patient begins breathing twice as fast.

explanation: If a patient has productive phlegm, they need to cough it out! Suppressing that reflex traps the gunk inside and can lead to worse blockages.

question: What is the true purpose of doing an Apgar score in the delivery room?

options.A: To diagnose long-term brain disabilities
options.B: To see how well the baby is adjusting to life outside
options.C: To decide the exact second resuscitation must start
options.D: To predict future intelligence in school

explanation: Resuscitation actually starts before the 1-minute Apgar is even done! The score just helps us see how the baby is responding and adapting over those first few minutes.

question: Why is an embryo extra sensitive to harmful substances during the first trimester?

options.A: The mother's immune system attacks foreign embryonic cells
options.B: The placenta has not yet absorbed any maternal antibodies
options.C: Major internal organs are actively forming and organizing
options.D: Amniotic fluid volume is too low to cushion the tissues

explanation: Spot on! Because body tissues and organs are forming rapidly during this time (organogenesis), any harmful substance can easily disrupt their normal structure. You are doing great!

question: What is the main job of thiamine (Vitamin B1) in our cells?

options.A: It wraps around nerves to speed up signals
options.B: It helps brain cells turn glucose into energy
options.C: It stops white blood cells from overreacting
options.D: It carries oxygen through the bloodstream

explanation: That's right! Thiamine acts like fuel for the brain, helping cells process glucose so they can stay alive and active.

question: What is the main goal of nursing care for a patient with an irreversible, end-stage illness at home?

options.A: Administering experimental curative medications
options.B: Transferring the patient to a busy surgical intensive care unit
options.C: Performing aggressive cardiopulmonary resuscitation continuously
options.D: Providing comfort, pain relief, and emotional support

explanation: When cure isn't possible, palliative care focuses on keeping the patient comfortable, managing pain, and preserving dignity.

question: A patient cannot wrinkle their forehead or smile evenly on the right side of their face. Which cranial nerve is likely affected?

options.A: Cranial Nerve III
options.B: Cranial Nerve V
options.C: Cranial Nerve VII
options.D: Cranial Nerve XII

explanation: Cranial Nerve VII is the facial nerve! It powers all our facial expressions, so trouble here leads to a drooping or asymmetrical smile.

question: Why is long-term follow-up education crucial for a woman who had gestational diabetes during her pregnancy?

options.A: She has a significantly increased lifetime risk of developing Type 2 diabetes
options.B: She will automatically develop pregestational diabetes in all future pregnancies
options.C: Her pancreatic beta-cells will continue to destroy themselves over time
options.D: Her baby will permanently require blood glucose monitoring into adulthood

explanation: Gestational diabetes serves as an early warning sign for future metabolic disease, making ongoing lifestyle counseling and periodic blood sugar screening essential. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T006#GNS226_U4_T006_h8)

question: Which of these common phrases should a nurse avoid saying to someone who is grieving?

options.A: I am here for you whenever you want to talk
options.B: I am so sorry for your loss
options.C: Time heals all wounds
options.D: It is okay to cry if you need to

explanation: Phrases like 'time heals all wounds' can feel dismissive and unhelpful. Instead, just let them know you are there for them.

question: A client vomits twenty minutes after taking her emergency contraceptive pill. What should you do?

options.A: Ignore the vomiting because it has no effect on the medication
options.B: Consult the provider to see if a repeat dose is needed
options.C: Give her a high dose of intravenous antibiotics immediately
options.D: Tell her the pill failed and she must schedule surgery

explanation: If she vomits shortly after taking the pill (within two hours), her body might not have absorbed the medicine. Always check with the clinician if she needs another dose!

question: Why can't a nurse officially diagnose a patient with diabetes based on just one high random blood sugar test?

options.A: Glucometers cannot measure glucose above 150 mg/dL
options.B: Blood sugar levels never stay high for long periods
options.C: It is a screening test and needs confirmatory tests
options.D: Only laboratory nurses are allowed to make a diagnosis

explanation: Meals, stress, and illness can cause temporary spikes. Doctors rely on fasting tests or HbA1c to make a formal diagnosis.

question: Why are pregnant women advised to drink fluids between meals rather than during meals?

options.A: To keep stomach acid completely inactive during digestion
options.B: To prevent over-stretching the stomach which can trigger vomiting
options.C: To ensure the body absorbs all the vitamins from the solid food
options.D: To stop the kidneys from working too hard after eating

explanation: Filling the stomach with both food and large amounts of liquid at the same time increases pressure and promotes vomiting. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T012#GNS226_U2_T012_h4)

question: Which of the following is a classic example of a prerenal cause of acute kidney injury?

options.A: Direct toxicity to the kidney tubules from certain drugs
options.B: Severe inflammation of the glomeruli inside the kidney
options.C: A large kidney stone blocking the ureter completely
options.D: Severe dehydration from heavy vomiting and diarrhea

explanation: Prerenal causes involve a lack of adequate blood flow to the kidneys, often due to fluid loss like severe dehydration or shock. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T6#GNS213_U4_T6_h2)

question: When a heart valve is narrowed and blocked, what kind of extra strain does it put on the heart?

options.A: Electrical overload
options.B: Perfusion overload
options.C: Volume overload
options.D: Pressure overload

explanation: When a valve is narrowed, the heart has to push much harder to squeeze blood through it. That extra resistance creates a pressure overload!

question: Which sign is a major red flag for a developing perineal hematoma after delivery?

options.A: Severe, sharp pelvic pain out of proportion to the wound
options.B: Sudden high fever accompanied by shaking chills
options.C: Complete absence of lochia discharge for several days
options.D: Inability to feel the urge to urinate or empty the bladder

explanation: A hematoma is a hidden pool of blood building up under the tissues. It creates intense, throbbing pressure that feels way worse than a normal sore stitch.

question: Where do focal onset seizures originate in the brain?

options.A: Across both brain hemispheres simultaneously
options.B: In a specific, localized area of one hemisphere
options.C: Exclusively in the brainstem and spinal cord
options.D: In the peripheral nerves of the limbs

explanation: Focal seizures start in one distinct region of the brain, unlike generalized seizures which affect both hemispheres right away. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T16#GNS222_U3_T16_h3)

question: What is the primary difference between hypovolemic shock and cardiogenic shock?

options.A: Cardiogenic shock is caused by severe allergic reactions
options.B: Hypovolemic shock is caused by a blocked pulmonary artery
options.C: Cardiogenic shock involves heart pump failure, while hypovolemic shock involves fluid loss
options.D: Hypovolemic shock always features a very slow heart rate

explanation: In cardiogenic shock, blood volume is normal, but the heart muscle is too weak to pump it; in hypovolemic shock, the pump is fine, but volume is missing. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T5#GNS123_U3_T5_h4)

question: A community nurse shares treated mosquito nets during a malaria surge. Which part of the epidemiological triangle is this targeting?

options.A: The internal incubation period
options.B: The host's genetic makeup
options.C: The infectious agent directly inside the blood
options.D: The environment

explanation: Nets change the surroundings where humans and mosquitoes meet, which means we are modifying the environment to block transmission.

question: In clinical nursing, what is a 'toxidrome'?

options.A: An antidote given to reverse the effects of a specific snake venom
options.B: A group of signs and symptoms pointing to a specific class of poison
options.C: The physical damage caused by corrosive chemicals on the skin
options.D: The laboratory test used to measure blood alcohol concentration

explanation: Think of a toxidrome as a symptom 'syndrome' caused by a 'toxic' substance. It helps nurses quickly spot what kind of poison is at play!

question: What is required when a nurse needs to discard a leftover portion of liquid morphine?

options.A: The hospital pharmacist must inspect the empty syringe
options.B: Another nurse must witness and co-sign the disposal
options.C: The patient must sign a form confirming the waste
options.D: The nurse can throw it away alone at the end of the shift

explanation: A second witness prevents falsification and ensures leftover drugs are not diverted for illegal use. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T13#GNS122_U1_T13_h6)

question: Which heart chamber is most frequently injured in penetrating chest trauma due to its front-facing position?

options.A: Left atrium
options.B: Left ventricle
options.C: Right atrium
options.D: Right ventricle

explanation: The right ventricle sits directly behind the sternum, making it the most exposed and frequently injured chamber when sharp or high-speed objects penetrate the chest. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T9#GNS213_U1_T9_h2)

question: What is the primary difference between blunt and penetrating genitourinary trauma?

options.A: Penetrating trauma is caused exclusively by sports-related accidents.
options.B: Blunt trauma always requires immediate emergency surgery.
options.C: Penetrating trauma involves objects breaking through the skin and organ walls.
options.D: Blunt trauma only affects the kidneys and never the external genitalia.

explanation: Penetrating trauma is defined by a foreign object like a knife or bullet entering the body, whereas blunt trauma results from compressive force without an open wound. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T10#GNS213_U4_T10_h1)

question: Which single cranial nerve carries most of the parasympathetic signals to the chest and tummy organs?

options.A: Optic nerve
options.B: Vagus nerve
options.C: Hypoglossal nerve
options.D: Trigeminal nerve

explanation: The vagus nerve (Cranial Nerve X) is the main highway for parasympathetic signals, carrying about three-quarters of all outgoing signals to your internal organs. Excellent recall!

question: Why is organogenesis (organ formation) a time of high vulnerability for the embryo?

options.A: Major body organs are rapidly forming and can be easily disrupted by harmful agents
options.B: The mother's immune system attacks the organs because they are immature
options.C: The placenta has not yet formed to provide any nutrients to the cells
options.D: Cells stop dividing entirely during this phase to rest and repair themselves

explanation: Because body structures are actively being sculpted during this window, harmful substances (teratogens) can easily cause permanent damage. This is why early prenatal care advice is so crucial!

question: You smell smoke in a hallway during a home visit and reach a closed door that feels very hot to the touch. What should you do?

options.A: Open the door quickly to let the heat escape outside
options.B: Spray water directly against the wooden surface of the door
options.C: Break the door down to check for flames inside
options.D: Keep the door closed and use an alternate escape route

explanation: A hot door means a fierce fire is raging right behind it. Opening it could cause a sudden explosion of flames, so use another way out!

question: What condition often develops if Wernicke encephalopathy is left untreated?

options.A: Rheumatoid arthritis
options.B: Chronic kidney failure
options.C: Type 2 diabetes
options.D: Korsakoff syndrome

explanation: That's correct! If Wernicke's isn't caught and treated, it often rolls into Korsakoff syndrome, which brings long-term memory troubles.

question: Which device is best suited for automatically sending daily blood glucose readings to a nurse?

options.A: A remote patient monitoring device
options.B: An ordinary paper nursing notepad
options.C: A standard mercury sphygmomanometer
options.D: A hospital bedside surgical tray

explanation: Remote monitoring tools are designed to track and transmit vital health metrics directly to healthcare providers. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T12#GNS212_U4_T12_h2)

question: Why must a nurse check a patient's medication list before starting them on calcium supplements?

options.A: Calcium completely neutralizes the effects of all known blood pressure medications.
options.B: Calcium interferes with the liver enzymes that process daily vitamins.
options.C: Calcium increases the rate at which the kidneys excrete water-soluble drugs.
options.D: Calcium can bind to certain antibiotics in the gut and stop them from working.

explanation: Spot on! Calcium binds with certain drugs (like tetracyclines) in the stomach, forming a combo your body can't absorb. Always check for drug interactions!

question: What do we call the reply a listener gives back to a speaker during a chat?

options.A: Encoding
options.B: The channel
options.C: Feedback
options.D: Decoding

explanation: That's right! Feedback is simply the response that lets you know if the other person truly caught your message.

question: What is the standard time frame following the end of a pregnancy for a death to be classified as a maternal death?

options.A: Within 6 months
options.B: Within 7 days
options.C: Within 42 days
options.D: Within 1 year

explanation: A maternal death includes any death occurring during pregnancy or within 42 days following the termination of the pregnancy, provided it is related to the pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T016#GNS226_U1_T016_h1)

question: Why does the electrical signal take a short pause at the AV node?

options.A: To stop signals from going backward into the lungs
options.B: To slow down the heart rate during sleep
options.C: To give the SA node time to rest
options.D: To let the ventricles fill up completely with blood first

explanation: That tiny pause is super smart design! It ensures the top chambers finish emptying their blood down into the bottom chambers before the bottom chambers squeeze.

question: What critical warning signs should a nurse teach a post-abortion client before she leaves the clinic?

options.A: Slight breast tenderness in the morning
options.B: Severe pelvic pain, heavy bleeding, or high fever
options.C: A temporary change in her favorite foods
options.D: Mild fatigue and slight spotting for two days

explanation: These symptoms are red flags that can indicate infection, retained tissue, or other complications requiring immediate medical evaluation. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h7)

question: What is the main reason for doing a pelvic ultrasound when post-abortion complications are suspected?

options.A: To determine the patient's exact psychological state
options.B: To check for retained products of conception or free fluid
options.C: To test for specific bacterial strains causing infection
options.D: To measure the patient's exact blood clotting time

explanation: An ultrasound gives doctors a clear 'window' inside to check if any pregnancy tissue was left behind or if fluid leaked where it shouldn't.

question: When is the best time to start palliative care for someone with a serious illness?

options.A: After the patient is discharged to a nursing home
options.B: Exclusively during the final twenty-four hours of life
options.C: Early in the disease process alongside curative treatments
options.D: Only when all curative treatments have failed

explanation: Great thinking! Palliative care isn't just for the very end. It works best when started right alongside regular medical treatments from the time of diagnosis to support the patient all through their journey.

question: Which bone forms the front boundary of the pelvic floor?

options.A: Coccyx
options.B: Pubic symphysis
options.C: Iliac crest
options.D: Ischial tuberosity

explanation: Great job! The pubic symphysis sits right at the front, marking the anterior boundary of the pelvis. You've got this!

question: How do A-delta nerve fibers behave differently from C nerve fibers?

options.A: A-delta fibers only react to emotional stress
options.B: A-delta fibers only work inside the brain and spinal cord
options.C: A-delta fibers carry dull aches over a long time
options.D: A-delta fibers are wrapped in myelin and carry sharp pain very quickly

explanation: Because A-delta fibers have a protective coating (myelin), they rush the message to your brain, giving you that immediate sharp sting right when you get hurt.

question: Why does a hospital admission often disrupt a patient's ability to meet basic human needs?

options.A: Hospital environments completely eliminate stress
options.B: Patients no longer care about their personal health
options.C: Familiar daily routines and independence are interrupted
options.D: Healthcare providers automatically handle all needs instantly

explanation: Being in an unfamiliar hospital setting takes away a person's normal independence, making basic tasks harder to manage alone. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h1)

question: How does a flannel graph help you out during a community health talk?

options.A: By measuring the blood pressure of clients during community outreaches
options.B: By printing thousands of takeaway leaflets for mothers attending the clinic
options.C: By allowing the nurse to move felt illustrations on a board to tell an interactive story
options.D: By broadcasting recorded audio messages across the entire village square

explanation: Flannel graphs use fuzzy cut-outs that stick to a board. As you talk, you can move them around to build a fun, visual story with your audience!

question: Which pelvic shape is the best and most normal for a smooth vaginal delivery?

options.A: Android
options.B: Platypelloid
options.C: Gynecoid
options.D: Anthropoid

explanation: The gynecoid pelvis is the classic female shape—nice, rounded, and roomy, making it ideal for childbirth!

question: A patient on chemo for bone sarcoma has a temperature of 38.5°C and chills. What is your priority nursing action?

options.A: Encourage the patient to put on a heavy sweater and drink hot tea
options.B: Administer a dose of routine oral pain medication for the chills
options.C: Notify the healthcare provider immediately for potential neutropenic sepsis
options.D: Document the finding in the chart and recheck the temperature in six hours

explanation: Chemo lowers white blood cells, making fever a true medical emergency. Always report it right away to protect your patient from sepsis!

question: Which item should be counted as part of a patient's fluid intake?

options.A: An intramuscular pain injection
options.B: An intravenous blood transfusion
options.C: A solid tablet pain medication
options.D: A dry solid piece of toast

explanation: Blood products and IV fluids introduce liquid directly into the vascular system and must be counted as intake. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T19#GNS122_U1_T19_h3)

question: What is the main benefit of placing a severe COVID-19 patient in the prone position (lying on their stomach)?

options.A: It improves oxygen exchange and lung expansion
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for intravenous lines
options.C: It prevents the patient from coughing during sleep
options.D: It allows the patient to feed themselves more easily

explanation: Well done! Gravity helps open up parts of the lungs that are pressed down when lying on the back, making it much easier for the patient to get oxygen.

question: What is the primary reason for performing meticulous pin site care on a patient with skeletal traction?

options.A: To encourage faster healing of torn skin ligaments
options.B: To keep the traction weights from touching the floor
options.C: To stop the metal pins from slipping out of the bone
options.D: To prevent dangerous bone infections like osteomyelitis

explanation: Pin sites create a direct open route from the environment to the bone, making rigorous sterile cleaning vital to stop bacterial invasion. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T7#GNS221_U1_T7_h4)

question: What is the best way to walk down the hall with a patient who has a visual impairment?

options.A: Walk behind the client and verbally give step-by-step directions
options.B: Walk side by side while holding hands tightly with the client
options.C: Push the client from behind by placing hands firmly on their shoulders
options.D: Walk slightly ahead and let the client hold onto your elbow

explanation: You've got it! Letting them hold your elbow while you lead slightly gives them physical cues for your movements and keeps them feeling secure.

question: Which test is most helpful for checking acid-base balance after an asphyxial event?

options.A: Arterial blood gas analysis
options.B: Routine urinalysis dipstick
options.C: Serum electrolyte panel
options.D: Complete blood cell count

explanation: An ABG test is your best friend here. It gives you a direct look at the patient's blood pH, oxygen levels, and how well they are clearing out carbon dioxide.

question: What is a major reason food gets lost before it ever reaches the local market?

options.A: Excessive consumer demand in urban centers
options.B: High levels of crop diversity on small farms
options.C: Poor storage facilities and bad transport roads
options.D: Strict government food safety inspections

explanation: Bad roads and poor storage mean a lot of harvest spoils before getting to people who need it. A very real challenge in many regions!

question: In community health statistics, what does 'incidence' tell us?

options.A: The total number of all old and new cases in a population
options.B: The percentage of infected patients who die from the disease
options.C: The number of new cases of a disease over a specific time
options.D: The expected baseline level of an illness in a community

explanation: Think of incidence as new arrivals! It counts brand-new cases popping up so nurses can see how fast an illness is currently spreading.

question: What is the main reason for using aseptic technique during surgery?

options.A: To reduce the cost of surgical supplies
options.B: To make the surgical room smell clean
options.C: To eliminate all micro-organisms from the surgical field
options.D: To speed up the recovery time after anesthesia

explanation: Great job! Aseptic technique blocks germs and bad bugs from getting into the patient's vulnerable body tissues.

question: What is a major advantage of longitudinal research over cross-sectional studies?

options.A: It never suffers from patients dropping out of the study
options.B: It can establish the chronological sequence of events and changes over time
options.C: It requires zero ethical approval from hospital boards
options.D: It takes only a few days to complete from start to finish

explanation: Correct! Because measurements happen repeatedly, we can clearly see which event came first and how things changed.

question: What is the first crucial step before collecting data in a new community?

options.A: Writing a final report for the federal ministry of health
options.B: Administering mass vaccinations to all children under five
options.C: Demolishing illegal structures that block drainage systems
options.D: Community entry and gaining the trust of local leaders

explanation: Without properly introducing the team to local leaders and gaining entry, residents may be uncooperative and data collection will fail. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h2)

question: Why is it dangerous to overfill a sharps container in the ward?

options.A: It slows down the disposal of regular paper waste
options.B: It increases the risk of accidental needle puncture injuries
options.C: It releases toxic fumes into the clinical area
options.D: It causes the plastic container to melt

explanation: Spot on! Sticking needles out of an overfilled box is an accident waiting to happen for nurses, doctors, and cleaning staff.

question: Patient, health, environment, and nursing. Why are these four big ideas so special in our field?

options.A: They represent the four core pillars that define nursing practice
options.B: They are required elements for hospital budget planning
options.C: They determine the legal penalties for medical malpractice
options.D: They outline the exact daily schedule for ward nurses

explanation: Spot on! These four concepts make up the 'metaparadigm' of nursing—basically, the big four pillars that every single nursing theory builds upon.

question: What do tests and scopes usually show in the colon of a patient with Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS)?

options.A: There are deep ulcers throughout the sigmoid colon
options.B: Numerous inflamed pouches are present in the wall
options.C: A large mass is blocking the lower descending colon
options.D: The bowel structure and lining look completely normal

explanation: Correct! IBS is a functional disorder. That means even though the patient has real symptoms, tests and scopes show no physical damage, ulcers, or tumors.

question: Which sterile instrument is used to gently hold and steady the cervix during an IUD procedure?

options.A: Sims speculum
options.B: Sponge forceps
options.C: Uterine sound
options.D: Tenaculum

explanation: The tenaculum gently holds the cervix steady and straightens out the angle of the uterus so you can pass the IUD smoothly.

question: Which global health body leads the way in setting standards for medical waste management?

options.A: International Monetary Fund
options.B: World Health Organization
options.C: International Labour Organization
options.D: World Trade Organization

explanation: The World Health Organization (WHO) provides the main guidelines and handbooks that countries follow to keep medical waste disposal safe.

question: Why is the risk of infection often lower in home care than in hospital wards?

options.A: Homes are chemically sterilized by professional cleaning crews daily
options.B: Home care nurses wear full surgical hazmat suits during every visit
options.C: Bacteria cannot survive outside of a traditional hospital building
options.D: Patients are separated from other sick individuals and hospital germs

explanation: Recovering away from shared rooms and hospital pathogens greatly reduces the chance of catching secondary infections. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h4)

question: What is the best nursing action when a dying patient talks about spiritual distress?

options.A: Prescribe an antidepressant medication immediately
options.B: Listen empathetically and offer to arrange a chaplain visit
options.C: Argue theological points to prove the patient wrong
options.D: Tell the patient not to worry about religious matters

explanation: Wonderful! As nurses, we support spiritual needs by being a caring listener and connecting patients with someone who can offer the right spiritual comfort.

question: How do major community accidents immediately affect local hospitals and clinics?

options.A: By eliminating the need for surgical supplies
options.B: By overwhelming emergency wards and depleting blood banks
options.C: By reducing the overall cost of running the hospital
options.D: By increasing the number of available nurses on duty

explanation: A sudden rush of trauma patients can quickly stretch hospital supplies, staff, and blood reserves to their limits.

question: What is the main cause of Respiratory Distress Syndrome in a premature baby?

options.A: A weak and underdeveloped heart muscle
options.B: An infection in the urinary tract
options.C: A lack of pulmonary surfactant
options.D: Swallowing too much amniotic fluid

explanation: Without enough surfactant to keep them open, the baby's tiny air sacs stick together and collapse. Knowing this helps you understand why we push for steroid coverage!

question: Which of these is a very common reason to perform a laparoscopy?

options.A: Extraction of kidney stones
options.B: Drainage of a cerebral abscess
options.C: Repair of a fractured femur bone
options.D: Removal of an inflamed appendix

explanation: Brilliant! Removing an appendix using tiny cuts (laparoscopic appendectomy) is a very common and safe way to treat appendicitis.

question: Which vital sign change usually comes with a widespread inflammatory response?

options.A: Elevated blood oxygen
options.B: Decreased heart rate
options.C: Elevated temperature
options.D: Lowered respiratory rate

explanation: Correct! Fever is a classic full-body response triggered when inflammatory signals talk to the brain's temperature control center.

question: Which type of drug crosses biological cell membranes the easiest?

options.A: Fat-soluble molecules
options.B: Water-soluble salts
options.C: Highly charged ions
options.D: Large protein molecules

explanation: Cell membranes are made of fats (lipids), so fat-friendly (lipophilic) drugs slide right through them without needing any special ticket!

question: A nurse is preparing to use a blood pressure cuff on a patient with unbroken skin. How should this item be classified and processed?

options.A: Semi-critical item requiring high-level chemical disinfection
options.B: Critical item requiring high-pressure steam sterilization
options.C: Non-critical item requiring low to intermediate-level disinfection
options.D: Sterile item requiring single-use disposal packaging

explanation: Blood pressure cuffs touch only intact skin, making them non-critical items that only need routine low or intermediate disinfection. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h3)

question: How do deficiencies in calcium and vitamin D primarily contribute to fracture risk?

options.A: They increase sudden blood pressure spikes
options.B: They cause muscles to pull too hard on joints
options.C: They stop the bone from forming a blood clot
options.D: They impair proper bone mineralization and strength

explanation: Calcium and vitamin D are essential building blocks for strong bone matrix; without them, bones lose their structural density. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T10#GNS222_U1_T10_h4)

question: Why does a weak immune system raise a person's risk for lymphoma?

options.A: Red blood cells lose their ability to carry iron
options.B: The bone marrow completely stops making platelets
options.C: Lymph vessels expand and trap toxins
options.D: The body fails to stop abnormal cell growth and viral triggers

explanation: When your immune system's security guard is sleeping (weakened), viruses and mutated cells can slip past and multiply unchecked.

question: What is the very first critical step after an injury happens at work?

options.A: Administering prompt first aid and stabilizing the victim
options.B: Suspending the supervisor in charge of the department
options.C: Filing insurance paperwork with government regulators
options.D: Interviewing witnesses about company safety policies

explanation: As a nurse, saving lives and giving first aid always comes first before any paperwork or investigations. You're thinking like a true nurse!

question: Why shouldn't a patient suddenly stop taking sleeping pills after using them for months?

options.A: It causes an immediate return of normal sleep patterns within twenty-four hours
options.B: It forces the liver to store toxic amounts of unabsorbed metabolites
options.C: It leads to permanent damage to the digestive tract lining
options.D: It can trigger severe withdrawal symptoms, including rebound insomnia and seizures

explanation: Stopping suddenly shocks the brain since it's used to the drug's help, leading to terrible withdrawal and sleepless nights (rebound insomnia).

question: Why are spinal reflexes important for the body?

options.A: They allow the brain to store long-term memories of painful events
options.B: They control conscious decisions made during physical exercise
options.C: They circulate nutrients through the spinal canal
options.D: They provide rapid, automatic responses without waiting for brain processing

explanation: Reflexes bypass the brain to react instantly to danger, such as pulling a hand away from a hot stove. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T1#GNS222_U3_T1_h3)

question: How do we view sleep in modern physiology?

options.A: An active, organized physiological state
options.B: A purely psychological phenomenon
options.C: A complete shutdown of brain activity
options.D: A passive absence of wakefulness

explanation: You might think the brain switches off at night, but sleep is actually a busy, organized state managed by specific brain networks. Great job keeping up with your physiology!

question: Which term describes an objective and measurable alteration in body function?

options.A: Disease
options.B: Wellness
options.C: Illness
options.D: Continuum

explanation: Disease refers to the pathological changes inside the body that medical tests can measure and detect. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T5#GNS123_U1_T5_h2)

question: A nurse washes her hands thoroughly with soap and water before entering a patient's room. Which group of germs is she mostly trying to wash away?

options.A: Resident microbiota
options.B: Systemic pathogens
options.C: Endogenous spores
options.D: Transient microbiota

explanation: Spot on! When you touch door handles or charts, you pick up temporary ('transient') microbes. Handwashing washes those casual hitchhikers right down the drain before you touch your patient.

question: How should a nurse respond to a patient who insists on getting an injection instead of pills for a mild illness?

options.A: Explain that oral medications are often just as effective and much safer
options.B: Tell the patient that injections are illegal for treating mild illnesses
options.C: Refuse to speak with the patient until they accept the prescribed pills
options.D: Administer a harmless saline injection to satisfy their psychological need

explanation: Patient education works best when it's kind and respectful. Clear up the myth about injections while highlighting why safe oral meds are great.

question: When should a patient with chronic pancreatitis take their prescribed pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy?

options.A: With every meal and snack
options.B: Only when eating foods high in sugar
options.C: Only when abdominal pain begins
options.D: Once daily right before bedtime

explanation: Spot on! Enzymes need to be taken right along with all food and snacks so they can mix with the nutrients and help the body digest food properly.

question: Which setting is a community health nurse most likely to visit when addressing occupational hazards?

options.A: Local small businesses and agricultural farms
options.B: Deep space research stations
options.C: National legislative assembly buildings exclusively
options.D: Private residential homes with no workers present

explanation: Community health nurses reach out to local workplaces like small shops and farms where formal safety officers might not be available. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h8)

question: Which hormone do the kidneys produce to tell the bone marrow to make red blood cells?

options.A: Thrombopoietin
options.B: Erythropoietin
options.C: Calcitonin
options.D: Melatonin

explanation: Brilliant! When oxygen levels drop, the kidneys send out erythropoietin (EPO) as a rescue signal to the bone marrow to make more red blood cells.

question: Which of these is a very common fall hazard found in many homes?

options.A: Loose scatter rugs on polished floors
options.B: Low furniture located near the walls
options.C: Hardwood floors without any coverings
options.D: Bright lighting in the hallway stairs

explanation: Exactly! Unsecured rugs easily slip underfoot, making them a leading cause of accidental falls at home.

question: Standard precautions must be applied to which group of patients?

options.A: Only patients with confirmed blood-borne viruses
options.B: Patients admitted to the surgical ward only
options.C: All patients regardless of their diagnosis
options.D: Individuals showing visible signs of a fever

explanation: Standard precautions assume any patient fluid could carry pathogens, protecting nurses and patients alike during every encounter. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T1#GNS311_U4_T1_h4)

question: Why is preparing a patient for common drug side effects an important counselling objective?

options.A: It guarantees that the disease will never return again
options.B: It allows the patient to sell extra doses to others safely
options.C: It prevents patients from panicking and stopping treatment early
options.D: It eliminates all biological reactions to the medication

explanation: When patients know what mild side effects to expect, they are less likely to abandon their prescription out of fear. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T7#GNS215_U4_T7_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of using a MUAC tape during a health assessment in an IDP camp?

options.A: To measure daily fluid loss from severe diarrhea
options.B: To estimate the total age of an infant accurately
options.C: To check for signs of chronic joint inflammation
options.D: To screen young children for acute malnutrition

explanation: MUAC (Mid-Upper Arm Circumference) is a quick, handy tool nurses use to check if a child is malnourished during emergencies.

question: How should you clean a patient's skin before giving an injection?

options.A: Wiping in a circular motion from the center outward and letting it dry
options.B: Applying an antiseptic spray and immediately inserting the needle
options.C: Wiping from the outer edges inward toward the center of the site
options.D: Scrubbing vigorously back and forth with a dry cotton ball

explanation: Always move from clean (center) to less clean (outward) to push germs away. Plus, letting the alcohol dry is what actually kills the microbes!

question: Why should nurses approach patient non-compliance with empathy instead of anger?

options.A: Because pharmaceutical companies require nurses to defend poor patient habits
options.B: Because judgmental attitudes automatically make patients immune to prescription drugs
options.C: Because non-compliance is usually driven by complex underlying barriers rather than simple defiance
options.D: Because hospital policies prohibit nurses from correcting patients who miss doses

explanation: Spot on! When we look past the surface, we find real struggles like high costs or confusion—not stubbornness.

question: Why are witness accounts particularly helpful during a nursing assessment for syncope?

options.A: Witnesses can provide a written police report of the accident.
options.B: Witnesses always know the exact medical diagnosis before doctors arrive.
options.C: Patients tend to exaggerate how long they were asleep on the floor.
options.D: The patient is unconscious during the event and cannot remember the details.

explanation: Because blackout involves loss of consciousness, patients rely on observers to describe if there was twitching, color change, or sudden collapse. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T16#GNS123_U3_T16_h5)

question: Why do nurses refer to pain as the 'fifth vital sign'?

options.A: It directly calculates the exact heart rate of the patient.
options.B: It can be measured using an automated cuff machine.
options.C: It must be checked and recorded alongside standard vital signs.
options.D: It is only relevant during surgical procedures.

explanation: Calling pain the fifth vital sign reminds us to assess and document it just as regularly as temperature or blood pressure. Great job keeping your clinical habits sharp!

question: A medical ward suddenly gets lots of new patients needing extra IV cannulas and dressings. Which budget item will go up?

options.A: Capital expenditure
options.B: Overhead revenue
options.C: Fixed costs
options.D: Variable costs

explanation: Spot on! Supplies like cannulas and dressings go up and down directly with patient volume, making them classic variable costs.

question: What is the most serious, life-threatening side effect nurses must watch out for when giving opioids?

options.A: Severe muscle cramping
options.B: Respiratory depression
options.C: Rapid hair loss
options.D: Sudden high blood pressure

explanation: You've got this! Opioids slow down the brain's breathing center, which is why checking the patient's respiratory rate is a vital nursing duty.

question: Why can carrying out a do-not-resuscitate (DNR) order sometimes be challenging in the ward?

options.A: Nurses have final authority to override any DNR request
options.B: Balancing legal directives, family views, and the duty to save lives is complex
options.C: Advanced directives are automatically the same in every culture globally
options.D: Doctors are legally forbidden from writing DNR orders

explanation: Exactly. Emotions, family expectations, and ethics often clash when dealing with end-of-life decisions, making communication very vital.

question: What is the main difference between an orthosis and a prosthesis?

options.A: An orthosis requires surgery, while a prosthesis is worn externally
options.B: An orthosis is electronic, while a prosthesis is purely mechanical
options.C: An orthosis is used only for children, while prosthetics are for adults
options.D: An orthosis supports an existing limb, while a prosthesis replaces a missing limb

explanation: Easy way to remember: an orthosis (like a brace) supports what's there, while a prosthesis steps in as a replacement limb. You've got this!

question: Why is it important to discuss proper medication storage during counselling?

options.A: Heat and moisture can break down drug potency
options.B: Expired pills turn into nutritional supplements
options.C: Refrigeration doubles the active dose strength
options.D: Plastic bottles attract dangerous insects

explanation: Improper storage in humid or hot places like bathrooms can ruin the chemical stability of medications. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T7#GNS215_U4_T7_h4)

question: What should you do right away if a patient says their eye pain and blurriness are getting worse during an irrigation?

options.A: Stop the irrigation and notify the healthcare provider
options.B: Turn off the room lights and leave the patient alone to rest
options.C: Increase the fluid flow rate to wash the pain away faster
options.D: Ignore the complaint because pain is normal during a flush

explanation: Never ignore worsening pain! Stop right away and let the doctor know so they can check for further injury or complications.

question: What is the main difference between the two sides of the Loop of Henle?

options.A: The descending limb performs active secretion, while the ascending limb performs filtration.
options.B: The descending limb is permeable to water, while the ascending limb is impermeable to water.
options.C: The descending limb receives blood supply, while the ascending limb holds lymph fluid.
options.D: The descending limb pumps out salt, while the ascending limb absorbs extra water.

explanation: You got it! Water flows out easily on the way down, but on the way up, the tube lets out salt without letting water follow.

question: An adolescent daughter tells the nurse she is exhausted from missing school to look after her sick mother. What should the nurse recognize?

options.A: The family is experiencing role strain and needs additional support
options.B: The teenager is simply misbehaving and needs stricter discipline
options.C: The mother's illness has cured itself through natural rest
options.D: Normal adolescent development includes full-time caregiving

explanation: When children take on heavy caregiving roles, it signals that the family system is strained and requires outside intervention. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a safe safety practice in the operating room?

options.A: Using smoke evacuation systems for electrosurgical units
options.B: Disposing of used scalpel blades in puncture-resistant containers
options.C: Wearing protective eyewear to shield against blood splashes
options.D: Recapping used injection needles by hand before disposal

explanation: Never recap needles with both hands! It is a major cause of accidental needlestick injuries and is strictly discouraged.

question: Besides the risk of physical infection, what immediate emotional impact does a needle-stick injury often have on a nurse?

options.A: Complete temporary paralysis of the affected hand
options.B: Immediate dismissal from their nursing position
options.C: Automatic immunity to all future bloodborne viruses
options.D: Severe psychological stress and anxiety while waiting for test results

explanation: So true. Waiting for screening results after a needle poke can cause a lot of worry and sleepless nights. That's why prevention is always your best friend! [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h6)

question: Why is directing considered more than just giving orders?

options.A: It requires ongoing interaction and support for the team
options.B: It eliminates all possible conflicts in the hospital
options.C: It replaces the need for proper nursing documentation
options.D: It focuses only on punishing staff who make mistakes

explanation: True directing involves inspiring confidence, communicating clearly, and actively supporting nurses rather than merely barking commands. [learn more](GST321_U1_T13#GST321_U1_T13_h1)

question: Why is writing clear and prompt nursing notes after a delivery so important?

options.A: It allows family members to review the delivery details at home
options.B: It replaces the need for verbal handovers between incoming and outgoing nurses
options.C: It ensures safe communication between shifts and provides a legal medical record
options.D: It is required primarily to calculate hospital billing and supply costs

explanation: If it wasn't documented, it wasn't done! Clear notes keep the whole healthcare team on the same page and protect you legally.

question: Which quick clinical bedside test is commonly used to check a patient's balance and stability?

options.A: Weber tuning fork test
options.B: Snellen chart test
options.C: Romberg test
options.D: Otoscopic examination

explanation: The Romberg test is a classic! You ask the patient to stand with their feet together and eyes closed to see how well their body maintains balance.

question: When should you apply a cold pack (cryotherapy) to a patient?

options.A: During the acute phase to reduce swelling and numb pain
options.B: To relax tight chronic muscles before a long walk
options.C: To relieve pressure on the spine from a herniated disc
options.D: To increase local blood flow in a healing chronic wound

explanation: Think of cold as a quick calmer for fresh injuries—it slows down blood flow to keep swelling down and numbs the area so it hurts less.

question: What happens when urine or stool stays on a patient's skin for too long?

options.A: Skin breaks down and forms painful sores
options.B: Skin changes color but stays strong
options.C: Skin oils heal the area faster
options.D: Skin gets tougher against germs

explanation: Spot on! Body waste is harsh on skin. Leaving it too long eats away at the skin barrier and causes painful bedsores.

question: Which set of vital sign changes makes up the classic warning sign known as Cushing's triad?

options.A: Low temperature, slow pulse, and normal blood pressure
options.B: High fever, rapid heart rate, and low blood pressure
options.C: Widening pulse pressure, bradycardia, and irregular respirations
options.D: Narrow pulse pressure, tachycardia, and deep breathing

explanation: You're getting the hang of it! Cushing's triad is a serious late warning sign that pressure inside the skull has risen to a dangerous level.

question: Why is taking off your PPE in the correct, specific order so important?

options.A: To ensure the equipment can be washed and reused for the next shift
options.B: To prevent transferring trapped pathogens from the gear onto your skin
options.C: To prevent the plastic straps from snapping during disposal
options.D: To speed up the process so you can leave the isolation room faster

explanation: The outside of your PPE is covered in germs. If you take it off carelessly, you'll end up wiping those germs right onto your face or hands!

question: Why must you as a nurse pay attention to a patient's feelings and emotional triggers during nutrition counselling?

options.A: Patients cannot digest food properly when they are sad
options.B: Psychology is the only valid study of human health
options.C: It allows the nurse to diagnose mental illness
options.D: Emotional habits can sabotage even the best meal plans

explanation: So true! If we only hand out diet charts and ignore the emotional side of eating, the patient will likely struggle with overeating no matter how motivated they look.

question: Why is understanding how drug classes work so important for patient safety?

options.A: It ensures the hospital pharmacy never runs out of stock
options.B: It allows nurses to manufacture replacement drugs at the nursing station
options.C: It replaces the need to check patient identification bands
options.D: It helps nurses anticipate overlapping side effects and drug interactions

explanation: Knowing drug classes helps you spot dangerous drug combinations or double-up side effects before they cause harm.

question: What is the primary medication class used as first-line treatment for minimal change disease?

options.A: Antivirals
options.B: Antibiotics
options.C: Corticosteroids
options.D: Beta blockers

explanation: Corticosteroids reduce inflammation and immune activity that damage the glomerular filter, making them the standard starting treatment. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T8#GNS213_U4_T8_h4)

question: What can happen if ear drops are administered while they are too cold?

options.A: Infection of the outer ear
options.B: Dizziness and vertigo
options.C: Immediate hearing loss
options.D: Swelling of the earlobe

explanation: Cold liquid near the eardrum stimulates the inner ear balance centers, triggering sudden dizziness and nausea. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T10#GNS122_U1_T10_h6)

question: Why is standing up slowly from a bed or chair especially important for patients with balance issues?

options.A: It ensures that the inner ear fluid drains out of the ear canal completely
options.B: It allows the heart rate to drop safely before physical exertion begins
options.C: It prevents permanent muscle cramps in the lower extremities
options.D: It gives the nervous system time to adjust and prevents sudden vertigo or dizziness

explanation: Moving too fast can trigger a sudden dizzy spell (vertigo) or a drop in blood pressure. Taking it slow keeps our patients safe and steady on their feet!

question: How should a nurse handle a patient who insists on a home delivery despite having high-risk hypertension?

options.A: Educate her on the dangers and firmly advise hospital delivery
options.B: Tell her to find a different nurse in another village
options.C: Ignore her blood pressure readings and let her choose
options.D: Agree to attend the home birth to avoid an argument

explanation: Patient safety comes first, so the nurse must use education and clear guidance to steer high-risk mothers toward safe facility care. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T9#GNS225_U3_T9_h8)

question: Roughly how many half-lives does it take for a stopped medication to be almost completely cleared from the body?

options.A: 1 to 2 half-lives
options.B: 10 to 12 half-lives
options.C: 4 to 5 half-lives
options.D: 20 to 24 half-lives

explanation: As a rule of thumb, after about 4 to 5 half-lives, less than 5% of the drug is left. Clinically, we consider the drug completely washed out by then!

question: What is the common name for the special area where two different cell types of the cervix meet?

options.A: The internal os cavity
options.B: The transformation zone
options.C: The fundal attachment point
options.D: The myometrial border

explanation: Spot on! We call it the transformation zone. This is a very busy area where most cervical cell changes love to start.

question: Why does cigarette smoking strongly increase the risk of bladder cancer?

options.A: Tobacco smoke reduces blood flow to the external genitalia
options.B: Carcinogens from tobacco are filtered by the kidneys and sit in the bladder
options.C: Nicotine directly damages the muscular layers of the ureters
options.D: Smoking completely stops the bladder walls from expanding properly

explanation: When someone smokes, the toxic chemicals enter their bloodstream. The kidneys filter these out into the urine, where they sit in the bladder and irritate the lining over time.

question: Why must a nurse always wear gloves when applying topical medications to a patient?

options.A: To warm up the cream before it makes direct contact with the patient's body
options.B: To prevent the patient's natural skin bacteria from contaminating the medication tube
options.C: To keep the patient's room environment completely sterile during the procedure
options.D: To protect the nurse from accidentally absorbing the medication through their own skin

explanation: Many topical drugs are potent and can easily pass through the nurse's fingertips into their own bloodstream if gloves are omitted. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T16#GNS125_U3_T16_h6)

question: When should you seal and replace a sharps disposal box?

options.A: When it is completely filled to the absolute brim
options.B: Whenever the outer cardboard gets slightly dusty
options.C: When it is three-quarters full
options.D: At the end of every single calendar month

explanation: Stop at the three-quarter mark! Waiting until it's overflowing invites accidental needle pricks.

question: Why is true primary nursing often difficult to practice in busy public Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: Severe staff shortages and high nurse-to-patient ratios make 24-hour individual accountability hard to maintain.
options.B: Patients in Nigeria prefer seeing a different nurse every hour for variety.
options.C: Physicians in Nigerian hospitals handle all bedside nursing duties themselves.
options.D: Nigerian nursing councils legally forbid registered nurses from writing patient care plans.

explanation: Real talk: managing a packed ward with limited hands means nurses often have to focus on quick tasks rather than continuous one-on-one primary care.

question: What is the main job of a pessary when treating pelvic organ prolapse?

options.A: To destroy abnormal fungal cells causing severe vaginitis
options.B: To permanently seal a vesicovaginal fistula
options.C: To physically support prolapsed pelvic organs inside the vagina
options.D: To replace lost estrogen in postmenopausal women

explanation: You're doing great! A pessary is a supportive device placed inside the vagina to hold dropped pelvic organs right where they belong.

question: What actually is sepsis?

options.A: The initial stage of viral reproduction in a host cell
options.B: A localized skin reaction caused by fungal overgrowth
options.C: A systemic, life-threatening response to an infection
options.D: A normal immune reaction during the prodromal phase

explanation: Correct! Sepsis happens when an infection gets out of hand, triggering a severe, dangerous full-body inflammatory response that needs emergency care.

question: Why do nurses prefer using a central venous line instead of a small hand vein when running continuous vasopressor drugs?

options.A: It prevents severe tissue damage if the medication leaks into surrounding tissue
options.B: It allows medications to bypass the liver and filter directly into the kidneys
options.C: It eliminates the need for continuous blood pressure monitoring
options.D: It increases the overall absorption rate in peripheral skeletal muscles

explanation: Vasoactive drugs squeeze vessels so hard that if they leak out of a small hand or arm vein into the skin, they can cut off blood flow and cause the tissue to die (necrosis). Central lines handle these strong drugs safely in big veins!

question: Why do health teams check 'signal functions' instead of just looking at hospital buildings?

options.A: To verify that actual life-saving treatments are actively being delivered to patients
options.B: To calculate the exact electricity consumption of hospital lighting
options.C: To determine the architectural layout required for nursing stations
options.D: To audit the daily cleaning schedules of delivery rooms

explanation: A nice building isn't enough! Signal functions prove that the staff, drugs, and equipment are actually there to save lives.

question: A stroke patient is trying to stick out their tongue, but it keeps pulling to one side. Which muscle is likely affected?

options.A: Palatoglossus
options.B: Hyoglossus
options.C: Genioglossus
options.D: Styloglossus

explanation: The genioglossus is our main tongue-poking muscle! When one side gets weak after a stroke, the tongue deviates toward the weaker side.

question: What is the main goal of a Performance Improvement Plan (PIP)?

options.A: To calculate the annual salary bonus for senior head nurses
options.B: To outline specific steps and support to correct performance deficiencies
options.C: To immediately terminate a nurse without a review process
options.D: To change the hospital's clinical nursing policies for all staff

explanation: A PIP is a helpful coaching tool, not a sack letter. It sets clear, achievable steps and gives you support to master any weak areas.

question: What is the 'harm reduction myth' regarding medicalised FGM?

options.A: The idea that cutting less tissue prevents all future pain
options.B: The assumption that older girls heal faster than babies
options.C: The belief that clinical FGM is safer and causes fewer complications
options.D: The theory that local herbs stop infections better than antibiotics

explanation: Some health workers wrongly believe that sterile tools make the procedure safe, ignoring the lasting harm. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h2)

question: What happens during Active Range of Motion (AROM) exercises?

options.A: The movement is done only while the patient is completely asleep.
options.B: A mechanical machine forces the joints to bend and straighten.
options.C: The patient moves the joints independently using their own muscle power.
options.D: The nurse or therapist moves the client's joints through space.

explanation: You've got this! AROM simply means the patient does the moving all by themselves, using their own muscles without any external push.

question: Why is early ambulation strongly encouraged after pelvic surgeries like a hysterectomy?

options.A: It prevents venous stasis and reduces the risk of blood clots
options.B: It forces the surgical incision to heal much faster
options.C: It restores immediate hormonal balance in the body
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for postoperative pain relief

explanation: Getting patients moving early promotes lower extremity circulation, significantly lowering the risk of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T7#GNS311_U1_T7_h6)

question: In everyday nursing, what do we mean by drug non-compliance?

options.A: A hospital running out of essential drug supplies
options.B: A doctor writing an incorrect prescription dosage
options.C: A patient failing to take medications as instructed
options.D: A pharmacist making an error during drug dispensing

explanation: You've got this! Non-compliance simply means the patient isn't following the exact timing, dose, or frequency the doctor ordered.

question: What is a key sign that a baby has pathological jaundice instead of normal physiological jaundice?

options.A: The baby feeding well and crying with a strong voice
options.B: Yellow skin fading completely by the end of the second week
options.C: Yellow color appearing within the first 24 hours of life
options.D: Jaundice showing up strictly on the third day after birth

explanation: Normal physiological jaundice takes a little time to show up. Any yellow color appearing on day one (within 24 hours) is a red flag that needs a closer look by the medical team.

question: What safety step is required if a patient experiencing cardiac arrest is lying in a puddle of water?

options.A: Turn off all nearby electrical appliances in the room
options.B: Double the number of chest compressions you deliver
options.C: Move the patient to a dry area and dry the chest
options.D: Place rubber mats under your own shoes while working

explanation: Water conducts electricity. Moving the patient to dry ground and wiping their chest ensures the shock goes through the heart, not out into the water.

question: What is the most important first step when treating a baby with acute diarrhea?

options.A: Preventing dehydration using oral rehydration salts
options.B: Placing the infant on strict intravenous nutrition
options.C: Administering strong anti-diarrheal syrups
options.D: Stopping all forms of breastfeeding immediately

explanation: You got it! Giving oral rehydration salts (ORS) replaces lost water and salts, saving the baby from dangerous dehydration.

question: How do rushed staff and chaotic hospital environments affect patients?

options.A: Patients demand longer clinical consultations
options.B: Patients feel intimidated and hesitate to question busy workers
options.C: Patients feel inspired to volunteer and help prepare medications
options.D: Patients report the hospital to international boards immediately

explanation: Correct! When a ward is super busy and chaotic, patients feel it's rude or risky to slow things down with questions.

question: What is the main goal of doing a slit-lamp examination?

options.A: To wash out dust from the lower eyelid
options.B: To get a close-up, magnified view of the front of the eye
options.C: To measure exact distance vision
options.D: To check the patient's full side vision

explanation: The slit-lamp shines a bright, magnified light on front eye structures like the cornea, iris, and lens so you can see them clearly.

question: What is a major plus of using comfort measures (like heat or rest) alongside medicines?

options.A: They guarantee the patient will have zero bleeding
options.B: They help reduce the overall need for heavy pain medications
options.C: They completely eliminate the need for any vital sign checks
options.D: They cure underlying infections without antibiotics

explanation: Combining simple comfort tricks with meds gives wonderful relief while keeping heavy drug use to a minimum. You're thinking like a holistic nurse!

question: Why do doctors sometimes prescribe a short-term anti-inflammatory drug right when a patient starts taking a new uric acid-lowering medication?

options.A: To permanently cure high blood pressure and chronic kidney disease
options.B: To prevent new uric acid-lowering drugs from triggering a sudden flare-up
options.C: To speed up the digestion of purines in the stomach
options.D: To completely replace the need for drinking water every day

explanation: You're doing great! When uric acid drops, old crystals start breaking down and shifting around. This sudden movement can trick the body into a flare, so extra protection is given at the start.

question: Which type of nerve pathway carries messages from the body up to the brain and spinal cord?

options.A: Efferent pathway
options.B: Afferent pathway
options.C: Autonomic pathway
options.D: Motor pathway

explanation: Spot on! Remember: 'A'fferent arrives at the central nervous system with sensory info from your body.

question: What does "process monitoring" evaluate during a community health campaign?

options.A: The exact financial profit generated by local primary health clinics
options.B: Long-term genetic changes in the community's disease risk profile
options.C: The total number of hospital beds required for severe stroke patients
options.D: Day-to-day activities like attendance numbers and media broadcasts

explanation: Correct! Process monitoring is just checking your daily checklist: Are the workshops running? Are people showing up? Did the radio jingle play?

question: How long does a seizure need to last to be called 'status epilepticus'?

options.A: Longer than five minutes
options.B: At least one full hour
options.C: More than twenty-four hours
options.D: Exactly thirty seconds

explanation: Any seizure lasting past five minutes—or happening back-to-back without waking up—is an emergency called status epilepticus. Quick thinking is vital here!

question: How does oxygen primarily travel through the bloodstream to body tissues?

options.A: Attached directly to white blood cells
options.B: Floating freely as pure gas bubbles in plasma
options.C: Bound to hemoglobin in red blood cells
options.D: Dissolved completely in blood platelets

explanation: The vast majority of oxygen in the body is carried by binding to the hemoglobin molecules inside red blood cells. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T6#GNS212_U4_T6_h2)

question: What do biological indicators test for when placed inside a sterilizer?

options.A: The total weight of the metal trays loaded into the chamber
options.B: The correct color change of paper tape on instrument packs
options.C: The actual destruction of highly resistant bacterial spores
options.D: The exact temperature of the room surrounding the machine

explanation: Spot on! Biological indicators use real, super-tough live spores to prove that the machine is strong enough to kill the hardest-to-beat germs.

question: Which temporary side effect is very common after taking misoprostol?

options.A: Complete temporary paralysis
options.B: High blood pressure requiring medication
options.C: Chills and low-grade fever
options.D: Severe permanent hair loss

explanation: You got it! Misoprostol frequently causes mild, temporary side effects like chills, nausea, or a slight fever. They pass quickly!

question: Why is it important for nurses to understand nutrient quantification?

options.A: To measure the physical weight of a patient daily
options.B: To determine the manufacturing date of packaged food items
options.C: To calculate the exact financial cost of hospital meals
options.D: To accurately evaluate dietary adequacy and plan patient care

explanation: Spotting what's lacking or in excess helps you build a killer care plan for your patients. Keep it up!

question: Why should a patient with peripheral arterial disease be told not to put a hot water bottle directly on their feet?

options.A: External heat stops blood pressure medications from working
options.B: Poor feeling in the legs makes it easy to get bad burns without noticing
options.C: Heat can cause surface veins to collapse permanently
options.D: Warm temperatures make plaque grow faster

explanation: Because bad circulation can dull nerve feelings in the feet, patients might not realize the water is scalding hot until their skin is severely burned. Good clinical safety knowledge!

question: In which situation should a routine paracentesis definitely NOT be done?

options.A: A history of controlled high blood pressure
options.B: Mild swelling in both ankles and feet
options.C: A slight elevation in liver enzymes
options.D: An acute surgical abdomen needing immediate operation

explanation: If a patient needs emergency surgery for an acute belly issue, a routine fluid tap is not appropriate.

question: An unmarried young girl comes to the clinic asking about family planning, and another nurse loudly criticizes her morals. What is the best way for you to handle this?

options.A: Ignore the situation because nurse-to-nurse conflicts are discouraged
options.B: Gently intervene, take over the client's care, and provide confidential, non-judgmental education
options.C: Agree with the colleague so the young girl learns a lesson about societal expectations
options.D: Report the girl to hospital security for seeking family planning services
